rule: Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), enum-variant/data construction (Rust `Some(x)`, `E::V(..)`, Haskell `Con {..}`), casts, language constructs (`isset`, `empty`, `sizeof`), declarations/function heads, module attributes, typespecs, field access without a call. | Dot-syntax property access is not a call.
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. No edge for: dot-syntax property set `self.name = …` and get `self.count` (Decision 2026-10-29: not a call, even though the runtime sends the accessor), struct initializer `{1, 2}` (data construction), `sizeof` (language construct), the C cast, `@selector(check)` (a method reference without a call), passing `helper` as a function pointer, the block literal bound to `unused` that is never invoked (a definition, not a call), @interface/@property declarations. respondsToSelector: is inherited from NSObject outside the scan → `Probe#respondsToSelector:` medium.
